about: What order the roles of a SYSTEM take, received rather than derived. A natural language is one kind of system and is deliberately not the schema: keying this on ISO language codes and WALS features would make the prior text-shaped, which is the failure specs/surprise-as-revision.md names as the remaining danger and which constitution II.1 refuses. A leitmotif has no ISO code and must still be addressable here.

provenance.method: HAND-ENTERED SEED across four modalities, chosen to span the order types the engine must tell apart and to prove the schema is not natural-language-shaped. Not a release import of any of its sources.
provenance.note: witness-tier throughout: every entry is an external fact about a system, injected and never derived from the material being read (SEED.md #1, constitution II.2). Each system names its OWN giver, because a prior is a gift per gift and not per file. Deriving these values from a corpus is a wall, not a hard problem — see eoreader6/scripts/EMBEDDING-FINDINGS.md for the measured attempt and its d = -0.37.
provenance.coverage: 13 systems across 4 modalities. Coverage is a fact about the gift, reported rather than patched: any system outside this list is a typed gap and must never be defaulted.

basis_kinds.surveyed: Observed across instances by a witness and reported as a tendency. A material that departs from it is MARKED, not malformed, and the departure is a finding.
basis_kinds.stipulated: Defined normatively by a specification. A material that departs from it is MALFORMED, or the system was misidentified. The two must never be conflated: the same disagreement means opposite things.

rigidity_kinds.fixed: The order is definitional. Any other order is a different thing.
rigidity_kinds.dominant: One order predominates; others occur and are marked.
rigidity_kinds.none: No order predominates. THIS IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN ABSENCE — it is what the giver found, and it is categorically different from a system this prior has never heard of.

nl:eng.name: English
nl:eng.giver: WALS Online (wals.info), Dryer & Haspelmath eds., feature 81A. CC-BY 4.0.
nl:eng.note: The configurational case: role rides on position, so reordering changes who did what to whom.

nl:eus.name: Basque
nl:eus.note: Role rides on case marking rather than position, so the same roles survive reordering. The contrast case for any extractor that reads position.

nl:deu.name: German
nl:deu.note: WALS codes German as having NO DOMINANT ORDER. This is the entry that makes `none` first-class: a system can be well attested and still have no single answer, which is a different state from one this prior has never heard of. An engine that collapses the two will report a confident order for every unknown system.

music:sonata-form.name: Sonata form
music:sonata-form.giver: Common-practice theory as codified in the 19th c. (Marx, Czerny); a description of practice, not a rule composers followed.
music:sonata-form.note: Here to prove the schema is not natural-language-shaped. The roles have no names in the material, no stable surfaces, and no lexicon — which is the omnimodal test (II.1) applied to this prior rather than argued about.

music:blues-12bar.name: Twelve-bar blues
music:blues-12bar.giver: Standard chord-progression convention as documented in jazz/blues pedagogy.
music:blues-12bar.note: An order convention whose sequence is longer than its role inventory — roles recur. Any consumer that assumes order.length === roles.length is text-shaped by accident.

music:cadence-authentic.name: Authentic cadence
music:cadence-authentic.note: The smallest real slot expectation: the position after the dominant knows its KIND and not its voicing.

code:json.name: JSON
code:json.note: STIPULATED, not surveyed. A departure here is malformed input or a misidentified system — never a marked variant, and never a finding about style.

tabular:tidy-observation.name: Tidy data observation row
tabular:tidy-observation.giver: Wickham (2014), Tidy Data — one observation per row, one variable per column.
tabular:tidy-observation.note: role_marking is `label`, not `position` — a tidy table's columns carry their roles in their names, so column order is genuinely free. The tabular analogue of a case-marked language, and the reason `role_marking` is a field rather than an assumption.
